get.description: Events in order, `limit` at a time. Pass `next_after_seq` as `after_seq` to read on.
Re-walk the whole chain. `ok` is true, or `broken_seq` names the first row that fails.
The latest balance per currency, as the worker last copied it from Airwallex. No rows: nothing ingested yet.

Receivables (open invoices) and payables due within `days_ahead` of `as_of`, overdue ones included.

`as_of` defaults to the date of the business's newest forecast, so "upcoming" is measured from the same day as the
numbers beside it; with no forecast it is today.

Stored forecasts, newest `as_of` first. Each carries its interval and the target coverage it was built for.

`latest=true` returns only the newest forecast per currency and horizon, which is what a dashboard draws. It needs
`business_id`, because "newest" is per business. `limit` and `offset` do not apply to it: there is one row per
currency and horizon, at most a few dozen.

Each value is the NET cash flow expected in the single week `horizon_weeks` after `as_of` (inflows minus outflows
in that currency), with an interval that should hold `target_coverage` of the time. It is not a running balance.

One business's invoices with their late-payment score. `order_by=risk` lists the riskiest first.

`late_risk` is null for an invoice that has not been scored (paid invoices are not scored).

post.description: Record a customer invoice. `notes` is untrusted free text: stored and returned as data, never interpreted.

Run the planner for one business and put every proposal through the policy engine.

Nothing is executed. APPROVE -> APPROVED, ESCALATE -> PENDING_APPROVAL, BLOCK -> BLOCKED. Repeating the call on
an unchanged state creates nothing new.
